layer_at_fault_line: The 'Substrate-independence × P5 interaction' row uses 'Pull, unaddressed' as a mark, but 'pull' is one of Step 5's eleven tests, not one of Step 6's eight marks (held, held if, two routes, loose, idle, borrowed, fixed, unknown); SKILL.md states 'a word from one list never stands in another's place,' so the mixing is the reader's own error, not a skill-wording push.
quotes: Support for test_remove: 'Remove it (suppose posthuman civilizations run on average only one or two ancestor-simulations) and the trilemma stops being forced — moderate f_P, f_I, f_sim all become consistent.' Support for test_swap: 'Swapped for wildly different figures (author explicitly tries several orders of magnitude off) and N_I stays "extremely large."' Support for test_pull and pairs_that_pull (P1|P5) and the mark-cell excluded from marks_per_part: 'Substrate-independence × P5 interaction | Pull, unaddressed | If minds can be simulated (P1) and simulations are common (conclusion of (3)), a careful simulated observer might expect some detectable trace (a "glitch") — which would itself be distinguishing information and disable P4. The paper doesn't test this pull; it simply asserts "the implications are not that radical."' Support for test_patches: 'No gauge is given for when this catch-all is or isn't swallowing the job.' Support for test_rival and rivals_built ('the doomsday argument's ssa'): 'the paper itself builds and dismisses the nearest rival (the Doomsday argument's SSA) by naming a real difference,' with the differentiating change given at P4's row: 'SSA needs random sampling across time; P4 only needs no info distinguishing you within a class at one time.'
